title.narrative: SCROL-R project: Championing effectiveness in addressing OCSE in Kenya

description.narrative: The SCROL Response (SCROL-R) project proposes a specialised capacity development solution targeting police officers from selected police stations in Kibra  and Dagoretti sub counties, Nairobi County. The two areas were selected to leverage on the work being done under the ongoing SCROL programme, and considering the commitment demonstrated by government officials in these locations. The primary target will be officers in police stations who handle child related cases.

title.narrative: Change in knowledge on OCSE among trained justice system actors

description.narrative: Change in knowledge on OCSE among trained justice system actors

comment.narrative:
Following the 4-day training on investigation and prosecution of OCSE cases, significant improvement in knowledge levels was observed among the 45 justice system actors (15 men and 30 women) who participated. Pre-test assessments revealed limited familiarity with specific investigative and prosecutorial approaches tailored to OCSE cases. Post-training evaluations demonstrated marked progress, with participants showcasing a deeper understanding of OCSE dynamics, victim-centered approaches, and the legal tools available to address such cases.
This measurable increase in knowledge highlights the effectiveness of the training in equipping justice actors with the skills necessary to enhance the response to OCSE cases, ultimately contributing to a more robust justice system.;
The formative assessment will determine the training to be done and therefore knowledge change will be measured during these trainings scheduled for August .;
This output will be evaluated and reported in the next quarter after the training of justice actors, scheduled to take place from 28th to 31st October 2024.;

title.narrative: Number of justice system actors trained to address OCSE.

description.narrative: Number of justice system actors trained to address OCSE.

comment.narrative: A total of 45 justice system actors (15 men and 30 women) were identified and equipped with specialized skills in investigating and prosecuting Online Child Sexual Exploitation (OCSE) cases. The training, which spanned four days from October 28th to 31st, 2024, focused on enhancing the capacity of justice system actors to handle OCSEA cases more effectively. Participants gained critical knowledge and practical skills in evidence collection, case management, victim support, and legal procedures tailored to OCSEA contexts.;

The training for the judicial actors has not began. This is due to delay in finalization of the formative assessment. The assessment was meant to highlight capacity gaps within the judicial system actors which the project will come in to address. These trainings are scheduled for August.;
This output will be achieved and reported in the next quarter after the training of justice actors, scheduled to take place from 28th to 31st October 2024.;
